independent_review_blocker.reproducer_A: gzip-valid, UTF-8-valid CSV body with a single field exceeding csv.field_size_limit() (131072 bytes) -- reproducer used: 200000-char field in a data row with an otherwise well-formed header/row shape -- raised bare csv.Error out of both materialize_parser_a (via rp.parse_daily_object's own unwrapped list(csv.DictReader(...)) body-row parse) and materialize_parser_b (via this module's own body-row csv.DictReader parse, previously outside any try/except)
independent_review_blocker.reproducer_class_B: TypeError: conversion from NoneType to Decimal is not supported
independent_review_blocker.reproducer_B: an unterminated quote in one physical CSV row swallows the remainder of that row (and would swallow further rows/newlines too, until EOF or a closing quote), leaving csv.DictReader's restval=None in every header column after the swallowed field for that row; qntylab.r1_retention_candidate.daily_primitive's own row-parsing try-block calls Decimal(row['size']) / Decimal(row['price']) / float(row['homeNotional']) / etc. unconditionally, and Decimal(None)/float(None) raise TypeError, which is not in daily_primitive's own (KeyError, ValueError, InvalidOperation) except tuple
independent_review_blocker.batch_isolation_consequence_A: in materialize_batch(items, materialize_fn), the csv.Error object at any position terminated the loop for BOTH parser paths; a subsequent valid object (C) was never attempted -- reproduced directly with valid/csv-corrupt/valid and corrupt/valid/corrupt/valid fixtures for both paths.
independent_review_blocker.reproducer_B_did_not_terminate_the_batch: unlike A, the TypeError case terminates only Parser B's single call for that object (it is not itself an object-level container-corruption exception escaping materialize_parser_b -- it was a crash INSIDE materialize_parser_b, still uncaught and still propagating out of that one call, and would still have terminated materialize_batch for that object exactly like A if left unrepaired); it is documented here as a structurally distinct, non-conflated failure class per the follow-up task's explicit instruction, not because its batch-termination effect on an unrepaired boundary would have differed.
independent_review_blocker.parser_a_was_unaffected_by_B: Parser A already has its own REQUIRED_ROW_FIELDS (timestamp, size, price, trdMatchID) row-rejection check (row.get(k) in (None, '') -> rejected_row_count += 1, continue) that correctly handles this exact malformed-row shape without crashing; only Parser B's daily_primitive lacked an equivalent guard for the None case specifically (TypeError, not KeyError/ValueError/InvalidOperation).

csv_error.frozen_vocabulary_match: CONTAINER_ANOMALY (same bucket as gzip corruption, invalid UTF-8, and truncated-header cases already declared in commit 3081118's own module docstring under 'structurally truncated CSV')
csv_error.reasoning: csv.Error from field_size_limit overflow aborts csv.reader/csv.DictReader iteration entirely -- it is a whole-object CSV-tokenization failure, not a single-row-skippable condition -- so it is classified with the other structurally-corrupt-container cases, not as a per-row PARSE_REJECTION.
csv_error.not_invented: no new anomaly vocabulary was introduced; ANOMALY_CONTAINER (qntylab.r1_retention_candidate.ANOMALY_CONTAINER, aka CONTAINER_ANOMALY) already existed and was already the disposition used for GzipCorruptionError/TruncatedCSVError/UnicodeDecodeError.

typeerror.classification: A -- malformed row that frozen parser semantics already require to become PARSE_REJECTION (ANOMALY_PARSE_REJECTION). qntylab.r1_retention_candidate.daily_primitive already implements exactly this disposition (reject the row, rejected_row_count += 1, append ANOMALY_PARSE_REJECTION, continue with remaining rows) for structurally-identical malformed-row causes (KeyError, ValueError, InvalidOperation); Parser A's own REQUIRED_ROW_FIELDS check independently corroborates that a row with a None-valued required field is contract-anticipated 'malformed row' territory, not container-level corruption and not scientific reinterpretation.
typeerror.why_not_C_or_D: not classified as (C) an implementation bug requiring a STOP, because the mechanism daily_primitive needs already exists in its own file (the try/except -> ANOMALY_PARSE_REJECTION path) -- only its except tuple is one exception class short of covering an already-anticipated row shape, and Parser A's own field-conversion guard in _redundant_field_check already treats TypeError as an ordinary, non-crashing outcome for the structurally analogous homeNotional/foreignNotional/grossValue fields. Not classified as (D) protocol-underspecified, because rejected_row_count / PARSE_REJECTION is an explicit, frozen, already-populated field/anomaly in both the contract and qntylab.r1_retention_candidate.ANOMALY_PARSE_REJECTION.
typeerror.not_a_broad_typeerror_catch: this module still never catches TypeError anywhere. The repair pre-filters row DATA (not exception classes) before calling daily_primitive, restricted to the exact fixed column set (timestamp, size, price, homeNotional, foreignNotional, grossValue) daily_primitive's own try-block numeric-converts unconditionally -- see _PARSER_B_NUMERIC_ROW_FIELDS in qntylab/r1_daily_market_materializer.py. A deliberately-injected, unrelated TypeError from inside daily_primitive (a genuine programming bug, not this row shape) still propagates uncaught -- verified directly (see no_generic_catch_safety_property).

csv_error_parser_b.change: restructured so the body-row list(csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(text))) parse -- previously OUTSIDE any try/except -- now runs inside the same try block as _decode_container(raw_bytes), and csv.Error was added to that block's except tuple alongside (rp.GzipCorruptionError, rp.TruncatedCSVError). typeerror_parser_b.change: before calling rc.daily_primitive(...), rows are pre-filtered: any row where row.get(k) is None for k in _PARSER_B_NUMERIC_ROW_FIELDS = (timestamp, size, price, homeNotional, foreignNotional, grossValue) is dropped and counted. daily_primitive is called only with the surviving rows (unmodified call, unmodified Decimal/OHLC/aggregation logic on those rows). After the call, the dropped count is folded into the returned rejected_row_count and ANOMALY_PARSE_REJECTION is added to anomalies (via sorted(set(...) | {...}), matching daily_primitive's own set-based anomaly convention) -- reproducing exactly the disposition daily_primitive's own except-block already produces for its other row-rejection causes, not a new boundary-invented outcome.
